edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Agnosce et mulierem, agnosce et nuptam, de testimoniis et corporis et spiritus, quae patitur et in conscientia et in carne. Hae sunt tabellae priores naturalium sponsalium et nuptiarum. Impone velamen extrinsecus, habenti tegumen intrinsecus. Tegantur etiam superiora, cujus inferiora nuda non sunt. Vis scire quae sit aetatis auctoritas? Propone utramque, immature compressam in habitu mulieris, et quae maturitate progressa in virginitate duret cum suo habitu, facilius illa mulier negabitur, quam ista virgo credetur. Tanta est adeo fides aetatis, ut nec habitu obstrui possit. Quid quod etiam hae nostrae etiam habitu mutationem aetatis confitentur, simulque se mulieres intellexerunt, de virginibus educantur, a capite quidem ipso deponentes quod fuerunt: vertunt capillum, et acu lasciviore comam sibi inserunt, crinibus a fronte divisis apertam professae mulieritatem. Jam et consilium formae a speculo petunt, et faciem morosiorem lavacro macerant, forsitan et aliquo eam medicamine interpolant, pallium extrinsecus jactant, calceum stipant multiformem, plus instrumenti ad balneas deferunt. Quid singula persequar? Solae autem manifestae paraturae totam circumferunt mulieritatem. Sed virginari volunt sola capitis nuditate, uno habitu negantes quod toto suggestu profitentur.
thought_title: Recognizing the Married and Unveiled Woman
pass_a_gloss: Recognize also the woman, recognize also the married woman, from the testimonies of both body and spirit, which she suffers in conscience and in flesh. These are the prior documents of natural betrothals and marriages. Impose a veil from the outside on her who has a covering on the inside. Let also the upper parts be covered, whose lower parts are not naked. Do you want to know what is the authority of age? Propose both, the immature one compressed in the habit of a woman, and the one who, having progressed in maturity, remains in virginity with her own habit; more easily will that woman be denied than this virgin be believed. So great is the faith of age that it cannot be obscured even by habit. What is it, that also our women, even by habit, confess a change of age, and at the same time, when they have understood themselves to be women, they are led out from being virgins, certainly laying down from their head what they were; they turn their hair, and with a more lascivious needle, they insert their hair for themselves, with their locks divided from the forehead, they profess their womanhood openly. Already they seek the counsel of their form from a mirror, and they soften their face with a lavish washing, perhaps even interpolating it with some medicine, they throw a cloak on the outside, they press on a multiform shoe, they carry more instruments to the baths. Why should I pursue individual points? But alone, they prepare their whole womanhood for public display. However, they want to seem like virgins alone by the nakedness of their head, with one habit denying what they proclaim with their whole demeanor.

pass_b_english: Recognize the woman, recognize the married woman too, from the testimony of both body and spirit, which she endures in conscience and in flesh. These are the original documents of natural betrothals and marriages. Impose a veil from the outside on one who already has a covering within. Let the upper parts be covered as well, whose lower parts are not naked. Do you want to know what authority age carries? Set both side by side: the immature girl compressed into a woman's habit, and the one who has matured yet remains a virgin in her own habit. That woman will be denied more easily than this virgin will be believed. Such is the credibility of age that not even a habit can obscure it. What is more, our own women confess the change of age by their very habit, and at the same time, once they have understood themselves to be women, they are led out from virginity, laying aside from their head what they were; they twist their hair, and with a more wanton needle they fasten it, parting their locks from the forehead to profess their womanhood openly. Already they seek the counsel of their appearance from a mirror, and they soften their face with lavish washing, perhaps even doctoring it with some cosmetic; they throw a cloak over the outside, they lace on a multiform shoe, they carry more equipment to the baths. Why should I pursue individual points? Their preparations alone, manifest as they are, parade their entire womanhood in public. Yet they want to pass for virgins solely by the nakedness of their head, denying with one habit what they proclaim with their whole demeanor.
